## Water and wastewater treatment operator — federal variant (P2)

*Function:* Operate treatment processes in responsible charge so that delivered water and discharged effluent meet their limits.

*X4 match:* `skos:closeMatch` (confidence 0.75, applies to: water treatment; candidate agent draft, evidence J). *Authority position (editorial):* regulated-party.

*Credential gates (issuer verified):* Drinking water treatment operator certification (Grades I-IV / Class A-D, state-specific) (required); Wastewater treatment operator certification (Grades I-IV) (required)

### Developmental and full performance — indicative band WG grade set by the federal wage system job grading standard (entry/journey/senior/lead) (not a classification criterion)

**Major duties (indicative % of time, agent draft)**

- **Operate drinking water treatment processes to meet water quality targets** — 17%
  - Adjust coagulant dosing from jar test results when raw-water turbidity, temperature or organic content changes *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Verify disinfection contact time against required inactivation values at each operating flow and correct shortfalls before water enters distribution *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Respond to a treatment upset by isolating the affected process unit, bringing backup treatment online and notifying the primacy agency *(needed at entry)*
  - Supervise automated process-control loops, overriding setpoints when analyzer readings conflict with bench tests or visual plant checks
- **Operate wastewater treatment and resource-recovery processes to permit limits** — 17%
  - Adjust aeration and sludge wasting rates using solids inventory, settleability and dissolved-oxygen trends to hold effluent within permit limits *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Diagnose a biological process upset from microscopic examination, foam, odor and settling behavior before laboratory results confirm it *(critical, needed at entry)*
  - Route peak wet-weather flows through the plant to protect biological treatment, recording any bypass or overflow for required reporting *(needed at entry)*
  - Operate anaerobic digestion and solids handling to meet biosolids pathogen-reduction and stability requirements while recovering digester gas *(needed at entry)*
- **Supervise automated and AI-assisted process control in environmental operations** — 10%
  - Run a treatment process in safe manual operation when automation or communications fail, adapting the manual operating procedure to conditions
  - Monitor automated control loops and alarms on a treatment process, checking automated responses against field observations of process condition *(needed at entry)*
  - Override an automated control action when process indicators show it is driving the system toward a permit or safety limit, documenting the decision *(needed at entry)*
- **Manage field sample custody and field quality control** — 10%
  - Complete chain-of-custody records for every sample from collection to laboratory receipt, recording each transfer, seal and temperature check *(needed at entry)*
  - Collect field duplicates, splits and blanks at the frequency the sampling plan specifies, labelling them so the laboratory cannot identify them *(needed at entry)*
  - Report field conditions that invalidate samples, such as broken seals, temperature excursions or holding-time breaches, before results are used *(needed at entry)*
- **Work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites** — 10%
  - Identify signs of potential hazardous materials at a field site, such as drums, stained soil, odours or unusual debris, before disturbing them *(needed at entry)*
  - Isolate an incidentally discovered hazardous material, establishing a safe distance and notifying the designated responder before any further work *(needed at entry)*
  - Wear the personal protective equipment the site health and safety plan specifies, checking its fit and function before entering the exclusion zone *(needed at entry)*
- **Protect operational technology at environmental utilities and facilities** — 10%
  - Maintain an inventory of connected control and monitoring assets with their network zone, remote-access paths and owner. *(needed at entry)*
  - Run an incident-response drill that switches a plant or monitoring network to manual operation, recording the time to a safe state and the gaps found. *(needed at entry)*
  - Review remote access to control and monitoring systems under the change procedure, removing access that is no longer needed.
- **Apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings** — 10%
  - Conduct a no-blame review of a near miss or incident with the people involved to identify contributing conditions and corrective actions *(needed at entry)*
  - Deliver a pre-work safety briefing that covers site hazards, controls, communications and the stop-work procedure for the assigned work area *(needed at entry)*
  - Design a unit learning-from-incidents process that links reporting channels, review triggers and pre-work briefing content
- **Practice within licensure scope and responsible charge** — 9%
  - Determine whether an assigned task falls within the scope of one's licence or certification, referring out-of-scope work to a qualified professional *(critical)*
  - Exercise responsible charge over subordinates' professional work, directing and reviewing it so that the sealing professional can attest to it *(critical)*
- **Manage a municipal stormwater programme to meet permit conditions** — 6%
  - Inspect catch basins, pipes and outfalls on a scheduled route, recording each structure that restricts flow for cleaning
  - Trace an illicit discharge from a dry-weather outfall flow to its source using field screening and system maps

**Factor 1 — knowledge required (draft language)**

- Knowledge of and skill in: operate drinking water treatment processes to meet water quality targets (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4). *Distinguishing.*
- Knowledge of and skill in: operate wastewater treatment and resource-recovery processes to permit limits (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4).
- Knowledge of and skill in: practice within licensure scope and responsible charge (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4).
- Knowledge of and skill in: supervise automated and AI-assisted process control in environmental operations (EMST target journey L2, senior L3, lead L4).
- Knowledge of and skill in: protect operational technology at environmental utilities and facilities (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3).
- Knowledge of and skill in: manage field sample custody and field quality control (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L3).
- Knowledge of and skill in: apply safety practices and stop-work authority across field, facility and incident settings (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L3, lead L4).
  - A no-blame incident review separates system and condition causes from individual error and sanctions only reckless or wilful acts, so that people keep reporting near misses.
  - Stop-work authority lets any worker halt a task they judge unsafe; the task resumes only after the hazard is assessed and the plan revised, and the person who stopped it is not penalized.
- Knowledge of and skill in: work safely on hazardous, industrial and energized field sites (EMST target entry L1, journey L2, senior L2, lead L2).
